A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same rank-1 Fisher/EWC research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original gradient-geometry experiments, model-size analyses and continual image-generation results on MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1k.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds VAE objective diagnostics, higher-rank Fisher comparisons and unregularized continual fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: The proposed mean-gradient rank-1 Fisher penalty and its combination with generative distillation remain unchanged in Equations 6–7. Section 3.3 expands the sampling explanation; the new VAE and higher-rank experiments are diagnostics and comparators, not new proposed method components.

E1.justification: The four datasets and class-incremental image-generation tasks are retained. ImageNet32 in the new Table 6 corresponds to the existing downsampled ImageNet setting. The VAE diagnostic changes model/objective conditions without identifying additional data or task coverage; its dataset is unspecified.

E2.justification: Appendix E.4 substantially broadens the comparison set with stochastic-power-iteration rank-2 through rank-5 Fisher baselines on CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST, plus unregularized continual fine-tuning on all four datasets. These test alternatives beyond the retained diagonal-EWC and replay comparisons. Despite mentioning ranks 1–5, Table 5 reports no separate power-iteration rank-1 comparator.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce VAE MSE+KL objectives with KL scaling of 1 and 10^-3, the leading-eigenvalue variance fraction, higher-rank configurations and a zero-regularization control. Existing dataset splits, image sizes, FID/forgetting metrics and benchmark training settings remain unchanged. Uniform timestep sampling is newly disclosed, not established as a changed procedure.

E4.justification: v1 examines replay removal and smaller UNet variants. v2 adds substantive tests of whether rank-1 dominance depends on the reconstruction objective, whether higher-rank Fisher estimates help, and how plain fine-tuning behaves without stabilization. Appendix C and Tables 5–6 therefore expand analysis of the central assumption and design choices.

E5.justification: Table 1 and Figure 4 retain standard errors over three random seeds. Table 5 extends mean-plus-standard-error reporting without documenting a new estimation procedure or run count. The new VAE and fine-tuning results provide point estimates. Corrections to uncertainty values in Section 5.1 are numerical-result changes, not changes in statistical practice.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add higher-rank and fine-tuning outcomes; Appendix C reports approximately 50% leading-eigenvalue variance for the VAE, 85% with reduced KL weight, and 99% for late-step DDPM. Table 1 is unchanged. Section 5.1 corrects ImageNet forgetting from 15.2±0.1 versus 31.6±0.2 to 15.2±4.8 versus 46.2±12.9, matching that table; this is not a new same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Assumption 1 now expresses linearity through a parameter-dependent operator A_theta rather than directly identifying the operator with theta, with corresponding revisions in Appendix B.2. Appendix C additionally qualifies the gradient-factorization argument for combined MSE+KL objectives. The propositions and main theorem remain, without a new general proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the quantitative ImageNet claim from forgetting being roughly halved to more than halved. The central contributions—rank-1 gradient geometry, inexpensive EWC and complementarity with replay—are retained. The conclusion still uses roughly halved.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds an MSE/PCA-based explanation and explicitly limits generalization to other objectives and nonlinear architectures. Section 3.3 explains why averaging across timesteps can remain useful despite early higher-rank structure. The limitations now discuss architectural components and regularization, while Appendix E.4 interprets higher-rank results in terms of limited power-iteration convergence.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies joint data/timestep sampling and uniform timestep selection. New experiments identify stochastic power iteration, the VAE KL scaling and the zero-penalty setting. Existing hardware, runtime and hyperparameter tables are retained. VAE architecture/data details and power-iteration budgets remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Vincent et al. (2010), Kingma and Welling (2014), and Ghorbani et al. (2019) to support the autoencoder rationale and VAE analysis, and removes Peebles and Xie (2023). The broader diffusion/continual-learning positioning remains stable. Consolidating duplicate Ho et al. entries does not remove a distinct work.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact. v2 expands Section 3.3, revises the assumption explanation and limitations, adds Appendix C and subsection E.4, and renumbers existing appendices. It also updates the publication header. These are localized additions and edits rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–6, moves Figure 4 and repacks the appendix learning curves across pages. Existing Figures 1–14 retain their graphical content, and Tables 1–4 retain their contents and basic structure. The presentation changes are limited additions and rearrangements.

improvement.justification: The added rank and fine-tuning controls strengthen assessment of the method, while the objective diagnostic and explicit qualifications better explain its applicability. Correcting Section 5.1 also resolves a numerical inconsistency with Table 1. The gains remain limited because the core evidence is unchanged and the new VAE and power-iteration experiments lack sufficient implementation detail for close scrutiny.
